title: Mild preferences, segregated towns
intro: Two groups of households start mixed at random. A household is content when at least a share 'want' of its neighbours belong to its own group; otherwise it moves to a random empty place. Find the mildest preference that still sorts the town into neighbourhoods of one group.
wantLabel: Share of like neighbours a household wants, want
similarLabel: Average share of like neighbours at the end
roundsLabel: Rounds until nobody wants to move
gridTitle: The town at the end (the two colours are the two groups)
checkMild: The preference is mild: want is at most 0.35.
checkSegregated: The town is segregated: on average at least 70 % of neighbours are alike.
